head: e9e35067fc3b419a54d790a71663071455f203f1
changes: Split consumed Config into its owned typed registry and a Copy descriptor of validated identities, assignment resources and cache settings.
Move the registry into the child typed session, removing the bootstrap registry clone. The coordinator discards its consumed registry and retains only the descriptor.
Replace growable configuration/session record vectors with fixed 248-byte and 312-byte arrays, preserving the v1 field order, little-endian words and reservation suffix.
Use the descriptor for context rebinding without cloning or rehashing the registry; retain the existing acknowledgement and reservation rules.
Replace the child ready record and four decoded reservation words with fixed inline arrays. Variable input/context/result packet storage remains separate.
limitations: No new GPU runtime or performance measurement is claimed. The four full-size GPU proofs and arithmetic coverage in the predecessor checkpoint were produced before this process-only ownership refinement.

Wire layout, registry identity, resources and proof arithmetic are unchanged. The native lifecycle suite validates child startup, context rebinding, dispatch, exit and reservation behavior with CPU reference fixtures.

Caller-held Config/registry copies, initial frame receive storage, dynamic context/request/result packets, queues, transport/driver/allocator/OS storage, stacks and complete worker/coordinator lifetime composition remain separate work.
Ordinary pool admission still rejects incomplete phase profiles; this change does not promote any workload or reduce resource reservations.
Nonempty-child full-size merges, broader workloads, paired performance comparisons, 24 hours AND 150 completed roots, multiple GPUs and AMD/Metal qualification remain required.
